name: Global Banking Policy Pack
description: DLP policy pack for global banks: payment card data (PCI), bank account and payment instructions (ABA, EU IBAN, global IBAN, SWIFT/BIC, wire vocabulary), customer PII across jurisdictions (US SSN/ITIN, UK/CA/AU/ZA and IN/SG/HK national IDs, EU and Asia-Pacific passports, dates of birth), customer records (statements, KYC/AML case files, loan applications), MNPI and deal information, confidentiality markings and private keys. Premised on Zscaler's predefined dictionaries: identification dictionaries are cloned at CONFIDENCE_LEVEL_HIGH (with 500-byte proximity variants) and the hierarchical EU IBAN / EU and APAC passport dictionaries plus the corporate-finance and financial-statement ML dictionaries are referenced directly. Reuses the ZBP Enterprise Policy pack engines (US PII, Financial Information, Private Keys) and their dictionaries under the same names, so the two packs share objects. Rules for Inline Web, Endpoint, SaaS Security and Outbound Email DLP plus containment (SSL decrypt, Cloud App Control, File Type Control, URL Filtering). Immutable: objects that drift from this definition are restored on the next deploy. All rules ship DISABLED at INFO severity (Zscaler's delivery convention): review, tune, then enable each rule and raise its severity.
references: Zscaler: Understanding Predefined DLP Dictionaries (CREDIT_CARD, ABA_LEAKAGE, SSN, USITIN_LEAKAGE, USDL_LEAKAGE, EUIBAN_LEAKAGE, PPEU_LEAKAGE, ASPP_LEAKAGE, FINANCIAL, ML_CORPORATE_FINANCE_LEAKAGE, ML_TAX_LEAKAGE)
Zscaler: Cloning Predefined DLP Dictionaries (confidence threshold, proximity, up to 4 clones per template)
Zscaler Best Practice enterprise pack (mkoyfman/zbp-automation) for the reused US PII, Financial Information and Private Keys engines
PCI DSS v4.0 requirement 3 (sensitive authentication data), GLBA Safeguards Rule, GDPR Art. 9/32, FFIEC IT Handbook
notes: Predefined identification dictionaries (CREDIT_CARD, ABA_LEAKAGE, SSN, USITIN_LEAKAGE, USDL_LEAKAGE) are cloned twice each: '- High' raises the confidence threshold to CONFIDENCE_LEVEL_HIGH and counts distinct matches; '- Prox 500' additionally requires a related phrase within 500 bytes, so a single match near context is enough.

EUIBAN_LEAKAGE, PPEU_LEAKAGE and ASPP_LEAKAGE are hierarchical predefined dictionaries (per-country identifiers). They are referenced directly at the tenant's default confidence rather than cloned, because a clone must list the country identifiers your tenant exposes (GET /dlpDictionaries/{id}/predefinedIdentifiers). To tighten them, clone in the portal at CONFIDENCE_LEVEL_HIGH with the countries you serve and point the engines at the clone; the policy pack will then report the engine as drifted, so update dlp_engines.json too.

Bank-IBAN (Global) and Bank-SWIFT BIC Code are custom pattern dictionaries anchored to phrases by proximity; the patterns alone would match ordinary text. Non-EU IBANs have no Zscaler checksum validation, so expect a few false positives from product codes near the word 'account'.

The two national-ID dictionaries are regex approximations (no checksum). Zscaler ships predefined dictionaries for many of these countries; if your tenant has them, replace the custom dictionary in the engines with the predefined name.

Bulk engines use 'more than 24 distinct matches' as the export threshold. Tune against real exports: a monthly statement run may legitimately carry hundreds of account numbers on a sanctioned channel, which is what the SaaS tenant scope and rule ordering are for.
If the ZBP Enterprise Policy pack is deployed as well, the shared ZBP-* dictionaries and engines are created once and reused by both packs; preflight shows them as 'already present'.

Every rule ships DISABLED and monitor-only (ALLOW, or report incident on SaaS). Nothing in the pack blocks; enforcing a rule is the customer's decision in the portal once incidents have been reviewed, and the journey records it as progress.
audience: Global and regional banks, card issuers, payment processors and wealth managers handling cardholder data, payment instructions and customer PII across jurisdictions.
when_to_use: The customer is a bank or payments company that needs PCI, customer-PII and payment-instruction detection out of the box, with KYC/AML, lending and MNPI coverage, across web, endpoint, SaaS and email. Start in monitor mode; enable the confidentiality-marking and card rules first.
